```python
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import (
    AsyncSession,
    async_sessionmaker,
    create_async_engine,
)
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase

from config import get_settings


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass


def _make_engine():
    settings = get_settings()
    connect_args = (
        {"check_same_thread": False}
        if settings.database_url.startswith("sqlite")
        else {}
    )
    return create_async_engine(
        settings.database_url,
        connect_args=connect_args,
        echo=False,          # never True in prod — SQL in logs leaks schema
        pool_pre_ping=True,
    )


engine = _make_engine()
AsyncSessionLocal = async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)


async def get_db() -> AsyncGenerator[AsyncSession, None]:
    async with AsyncSessionLocal() as session:
        try:
            yield session
        except Exception:
            await session.rollback()
            raise
```

```python
"""
Explicit input/output DTOs — no ORM entity is ever serialized directly.
Input schemas use extra="forbid" to block mass-assignment.
Output schemas are an explicit allowlist of safe fields.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import json
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Annotated

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, StringConstraints, field_validator

from models import Priority, TicketStatus


# ── Input ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

TitleStr = Annotated[
    str,
    StringConstraints(min_length=1, max_length=200, strip_whitespace=True),
]
BodyStr = Annotated[
    str,
    StringConstraints(min_length=1, max_length=10_000, strip_whitespace=True),
]


class TicketCreate(BaseModel):
    """Fields a caller may supply at creation time — nothing else."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")  # CWE-915: block mass assignment

    title: TitleStr
    body: BodyStr
    priority: Priority = Priority.medium

    @field_validator("title", "body", mode="after")
    @classmethod
    def no_null_bytes(cls, v: str) -> str:
        if "\x00" in v:
            raise ValueError("null bytes not permitted")
        return v


# ── Output ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class TicketOut(BaseModel):
    """Explicit allowlist of fields returned to callers."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    id: str
    title: str
    body: str
    priority: Priority
    status: TicketStatus
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime
    # owner_id intentionally omitted — no need to echo it back


# ── Pagination ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class TicketListResponse(BaseModel):
    data: list[TicketOut]
    next_cursor: str | None = None
    has_more: bool


class CursorPayload(BaseModel):
    """Internal structure encoded inside the opaque cursor string."""

    created_at: datetime
    id: str


def encode_cursor(created_at: datetime, ticket_id: str) -> str:
    payload = {"created_at": created_at.isoformat(), "id": ticket_id}
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(json.dumps(payload).encode()).decode()


def decode_cursor(cursor: str) -> CursorPayload:
    """Raises ValueError on any malformed cursor — caller maps to 400."""
    try:
        raw = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(cursor.encode() + b"==")
        data = json.loads(raw)
        return CursorPayload(**data)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid cursor: {exc}") from exc


# ── Error (RFC 9457) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class ProblemDetail(BaseModel):
    type: str = "about:blank"
    title: str
    status: int
    detail: str | None = None
    instance: str | None = None
    trace_id: str | None = None
```

```python
"""
JWT verification.
- Algorithm pinned to RS256 (never read from token header).
- iss, aud, exp all verified.
- Returns a plain dataclass — no ORM object, no DB round-trip for every request.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass

import jwt  # PyJWT >= 2.x
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer

from config import Settings, get_settings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
_bearer = HTTPBearer(auto_error=True)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CurrentUser:
    user_id: str
    email: str | None


def verify_token(
    credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials = Depends(_bearer),
    settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings),
) -> CurrentUser:
    """
    Dependency injected into every protected route.
    Raises 401 on any verification failure — same error shape regardless of
    failure reason (no enumeration of why it failed to callers).
    """
    token = credentials.credentials
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            token,
            settings.jwt_public_key,
            algorithms=[settings.jwt_algorithm],   # pinned allowlist — CWE-347
            issuer=settings.jwt_issuer,
            audience=settings.jwt_audience,
            leeway=settings.jwt_leeway_seconds,
            options={
                "require": ["exp", "iss", "aud", "sub"],
                "verify_exp": True,
                "verify_iss": True,
                "verify_aud": True,
            },
        )
    except jwt.ExpiredSignatureError:
        logger.warning("jwt_expired")
        _raise_401()
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
        # Log the reason server-side; never echo it to the caller
        logger.warning("jwt_invalid", extra={"reason": type(exc).__name__})
        _raise_401()

    user_id: str | None = payload.get("sub")
    if not user_id:
        logger.warning("jwt_missing_sub")
        _raise_401()

    return CurrentUser(user_id=user_id, email=payload.get("email"))


def _raise_401() -> None:
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
        detail="invalid_credentials",
        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
    )
```

## `rate_limit.py`

```python
"""
Sliding-window rate limiter.

Keyed by authenticated principal (user_id) for authed routes.
Falls back to IP for unauthenticated surfaces.

Uses Redis (atomic Lua) when REDIS_URL is set; otherwise an in-process
store (single-instance only — acceptable for dev/test, not for multi-replica prod).

NOTE: if a gateway (e.g. Kong, AWS API Gateway) already enforces per-principal
rate limits, set RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false and document that here.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import time
from collections import defaultdict, deque
from typing import Protocol

from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request, status

from config import Settings, get_settings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_ENABLED = os.environ.get("RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED", "true").lower() == "true"


# ── Backend protocol ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class RateLimitBackend(Protocol):
    async def is_allowed(self, key: str, limit: int, window: int) -> tuple[bool, int]:
        """Returns (allowed, remaining)."""
        ...


# ── In-process backend (dev / single-replica) ─────────────────────────────────

class InProcessBackend:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._windows: dict[str, deque[float]] = defaultdict(deque)

    async def is_allowed(self, key: str, limit: int, window: int) -> tuple[bool, int]:
        now = time.monotonic()
        dq = self._windows[key]
        cutoff = now - window
        while dq and dq[0] < cutoff:
            dq.popleft()
        if len(dq) >= limit:
            return False, 0
        dq.append(now)
        return True, limit - len(dq)


# ── Redis backend (production, multi-replica) ─────────────────────────────────

_REDIS_SCRIPT = """
local key    = KEYS[1]
local limit  = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local window = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local now    = tonumber(ARGV[3])
local cutoff = now - window * 1000   -- stored as ms

redis.call('ZREMRANGEBYSCORE', key, '-inf', cutoff)
local count = redis.call('ZCARD', key)
if count >= limit then
    return {0, 0}
end
redis.call('ZADD', key, now, now)
redis.call('PEXPIRE', key, window * 1000)
return {1, limit - count - 1}
"""


class RedisBackend:
    def __init__(self, redis_url: str) -> None:
        import redis.asyncio as aioredis  # type: ignore[import]

        self._client = aioredis.from_url(redis_url, decode_responses=False)
        self._script: object | None = None

    async def _get_script(self):
        if self._script is None:
            self._script = self._client.register_script(_REDIS_SCRIPT)
        return self._script

    async def is_allowed(self, key: str, limit: int, window: int) -> tuple[bool, int]:
        now_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
        script = await self._get_script()
        result = await script(keys=[key], args=[limit, window, now_ms])
        allowed, remaining = int(result[0]), int(result[1])
        return bool(allowed), remaining


# ── Singleton factory ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_backend: RateLimitBackend | None = None


def _get_backend(settings: Settings) -> RateLimitBackend:
    global _backend
    if _backend is None:
        if settings.redis_url:
            logger.info("rate_limit_backend", extra={"backend": "redis"})
            _backend = RedisBackend(settings.redis_url)
        else:
            logger.warning(
                "rate_limit_backend",
                extra={"backend": "in_process", "note": "not suitable for multi-replica"},
            )
            _backend = InProcessBackend()
    return _backend


# ── FastAPI dependency ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

async def rate_limit_dependency(
    request: Request,
    settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings),
) -> None:
    """
    Attach to routes via Depends().  Key is user_id when present (set by auth
    middleware earlier in the chain), else client IP.
    """
    if not _ENABLED:
        return

    # user_id is injected into request.state by the auth dependency
    key_value: str = getattr(request.state, "user_id", None) or (
        request.client.host if request.client else "unknown"
    )
    key = f"rl:{key_value}"

    backend = _get_backend(settings)
    allowed, remaining = await backend.is_allowed(
        key,
        settings.rate_limit_requests,
        settings.rate_limit_window_seconds,
    )

    # Always set rate-limit headers (IETF draft + legacy)
    request.state.rl_remaining = remaining
    if not allowed:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_429_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
            detail={
                "type": "https://api.example.com/errors/rate-limited",
                "title": "Rate limit exceeded",
                "status": 429,
                "detail": (
                    f"Limit {settings.rate_limit_requests} requests "
                    f"per {settings.rate_limit_window_seconds}s exceeded."
                ),
                "retry_after": settings.rate_limit_window_seconds,
            },
            headers={"Retry-After": str(settings.rate_limit_window_seconds)},
        )
```

```python
"""
Ticket endpoints.

Security properties enforced here:
- Auth: every route requires a valid JWT (verify_token dependency).
- Object-level authz: every query filters on owner_id=current_user.user_id
  (the predicate is in the SQL, not a post-fetch check).
- Rate limiting: applied via dependency.
- Input: TicketCreate uses extra="forbid"; owner_id comes from JWT, never body.
- Output: TicketOut is an explicit allowlist DTO.
- Pagination: keyset cursor, server-enforced max limit.
- Errors: RFC 9457 problem+json.
- Logging: wide event per request (emitted by middleware in main.py).

import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Query, Request, status
from sqlalchemy import and_, select, tuple_
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from auth import CurrentUser, verify_token
from database import get_db
from models import Priority, Ticket
from rate_limit import rate_limit_dependency
from schemas import (
    TicketCreate,
    TicketListResponse,
    TicketOut,
    decode_cursor,
    encode_cursor,
)
from config import get_settings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter(prefix="/tickets", tags=["tickets"])

Settings = get_settings()


# ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _problem(status_code: int, title: str, detail: str, request: Request) -> HTTPException:
    return HTTPException(
        status_code=status_code,
        detail={
            "type": f"https://api.example.com/errors/{title.lower().replace(' ', '-')}",
            "title": title,
            "status": status_code,
            "detail": detail,
            "instance": str(request.url.path),
            "trace_id": getattr(request.state, "trace_id", None),
        },
    )


# ── POST /tickets ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@router.post(
    "",
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    response_model=TicketOut,
    summary="Create a support ticket",
)
async def create_ticket(
    request: Request,
    payload: TicketCreate,
    current_user: CurrentUser = Depends(verify_token),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    _rl: None = Depends(rate_limit_dependency),
) -> TicketOut:
    """
    Creates a ticket owned by the authenticated user.
    owner_id is sourced exclusively from the verified JWT — never from the body.
    """
    ticket = Ticket(
        id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
        owner_id=current_user.user_id,   # from JWT, not request body
        title=payload.title,
        body=payload.body,
        priority=payload.priority,
    )
    db.add(ticket)
    await db.commit()
    await db.refresh(ticket)

    logger.info(
        "ticket_created",
        extra={
            "ticket_id": ticket.id,
            "owner_id": ticket.owner_id,
            "priority": ticket.priority.value,
            "trace_id": getattr(request.state, "trace_id", None),
        },
    )

    # Attach to wide event accumulator (see middleware in main.py)
    if hasattr(request.state, "evt"):
        request.state.evt["ticket_id"] = ticket.id

    return TicketOut.model_validate(ticket)


# ── GET /tickets ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@router.get(
    "",
    response_model=TicketListResponse,
    summary="List the authenticated user's tickets",
)
async def list_tickets(
    request: Request,
    cursor: str | None = Query(default=None, description="Opaque pagination cursor"),
    limit: int = Query(default=20, ge=1, le=100),
    priority: Priority | None = Query(default=None),
    current_user: CurrentUser = Depends(verify_token),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    _rl: None = Depends(rate_limit_dependency),
) -> TicketListResponse:
    """
    Returns tickets owned by the caller, newest first.
    Cursor is opaque and encodes (created_at, id) for keyset pagination.
    """
    settings = get_settings()
    # Server-enforces max; clamp silently (documented in OpenAPI description)
    limit = min(limit, settings.max_page_size)

    # Base predicate: ownership is always in the query — never a post-fetch check
    conditions = [Ticket.owner_id == current_user.user_id]

    if priority is not None:
        conditions.append(Ticket.priority == priority)

    if cursor is not None:
        try:
            cur = decode_cursor(cursor)
        except ValueError:
            raise _problem(400, "Invalid Cursor", "The cursor value is malformed.", request)
        # Keyset: rows strictly before the cursor position (newest-first)
        conditions.append(
            tuple_(Ticket.created_at, Ticket.id) < (cur.created_at, cur.id)
        )

    stmt = (
        select(Ticket)
        .where(and_(*conditions))
        .order_by(Ticket.created_at.desc(), Ticket.id.desc())
        .limit(limit + 1)   # fetch one extra to detect has_more
    )

    result = await db.execute(stmt)
    rows = list(result.scalars().all())

    has_more = len(rows) > limit
    if has_more:
        rows = rows[:limit]

    next_cursor: str | None = None
    if has_more and rows:
        last = rows[-1]
        next_cursor = encode_cursor(last.created_at, last.id)

    logger.info(
        "tickets_listed",
        extra={
            "owner_id": current_user.user_id,
            "count": len(rows),
            "has_more": has_more,
            "trace_id": getattr(request.state, "trace_id", None),
        },
    )

    return TicketListResponse(
        data=[TicketOut.model_validate(r) for r in rows],
        next_cursor=next_cursor,
        has_more=has_more,
    )
```

```python
"""
Application entry point.

Cross-cutting concerns handled here:
- Structured logging configured before anything else.
- HTTPS enforcement middleware.
- Trace ID injection (W3C traceparent or generated).
- Wide-event request logging (one JSON line per request, emitted in finally).

import logging
import time
import uuid
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, Response, status
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

from config import get_settings
from database import Base, engine
from logging_config import configure_logging
from routers import tickets

configure_logging()
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
settings = get_settings()


# ── Lifespan ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # Create tables (use Alembic for production migrations)
    async with engine.begin() as conn:
        await conn.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all)
    logger.info("startup_complete", extra={"database_url": "configured"})
    yield
    await engine.dispose()
    logger.info("shutdown_complete")


# ── App ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

app = FastAPI(
    title="Support Tickets API",
    version="1.0.0",
    # Disable automatic /docs and /redoc in prod — gate or remove them
    docs_url="/docs" if not settings.require_https else None,
    redoc_url=None,
    lifespan=lifespan,
)


# ── Middleware: HTTPS enforcement ─────────────────────────────────────────────

@app.middleware("http")
async def enforce_https(request: Request, call_next):
    """
    Rejects plaintext HTTP in production.
    TLS termination is the reverse proxy's job; this is the backstop.
    HSTS is set on every response.
    """
    if settings.require_https:
        proto = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-proto", "https")
        if proto != "https":
            return JSONResponse(
                status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
                content={"detail": "HTTPS required"},
            )
    response: Response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["Strict-Transport-Security"] = (
        "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload"
    )
    return response


# ── Middleware: trace ID + wide event ─────────────────────────────────────────

@app.middleware("http")
async def request_instrumentation(request: Request, call_next):
    """
    1. Injects a trace ID (W3C traceparent if present, else generated UUID).
    2. Stores user_id in request.state for the rate limiter.
    3. Accumulates a wide-event dict; emits one INFO line in finally.
    4. Attaches rate-limit headers to the response.
    """
    # Trace ID
    traceparent = request.headers.get("traceparent")
    trace_id = traceparent.split("-")[1] if traceparent else uuid.uuid4().hex
    request.state.trace_id = trace_id

    # Wide-event accumulator
    request.state.evt = {
        "event": "http_request",
        "trace_id": trace_id,
        "http.request.method": request.method,
        "http.route": request.url.path,
        "client_ip": request.client.host if request.client else None,
    }

    start = time.perf_counter()
    response: Response | None = None
    try:
        response = await call_next(request)
        request.state.evt["http.response.status_code"] = response.status_code
        request.state.evt["outcome"] = (
            "success" if response.status_code < 400 else "error"
        )
        return response
    except Exception as exc:
        request.state.evt["outcome"] = "unhandled_exception"
        request.state.evt["error.type"] = type(exc).__name__
        raise
    finally:
        request.state.evt["duration_ms"] = round(
            (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000, 2
        )
        logger.info("http_request", extra=request.state.evt)

        # Attach headers to response if we have one
        if response is not None:
            response.headers["X-Trace-Id"] = trace_id
            remaining = getattr(request.state, "rl_remaining", None)
            if remaining is not None:
                response.headers["RateLimit-Remaining"] = str(remaining)
                response.headers["RateLimit-Limit"] = str(
                    settings.rate_limit_requests
                )


# ── Global exception handler ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def unhandled_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
    """
    Converts ALL unhandled exceptions to a generic RFC 9457 response.
    Full detail goes to the structured log; nothing internal reaches the client.
    """
    trace_id = getattr(request.state, "trace_id", uuid.uuid4().hex)
    logger.exception(
        "unhandled_exception",
        extra={"trace_id": trace_id, "path": request.url.path},
    )
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
        content={
            "type": "https://api.example.com/errors/internal",
            "title": "Internal Server Error",
            "status": 500,
            "detail": "An unexpected error occurred.",
            "trace_id": trace_id,
        },
        media_type="application/problem+json",
    )


# ── Routers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

app.include_router(tickets.router, prefix="/api/v1")
```

```python
    resp_b = await client_b.get("/api/v1/tickets")

    assert resp_b.json()["data"] == [], (

async def test_cursor_pagination(client: AsyncClient):
    # Create 5 tickets
    for i in range(5):
        await client.post("/api/v1/tickets", json=_ticket_payload(title=f"T{i}"))

    # Page 1: limit=3
    resp1 = await client.get("/api/v1/tickets?limit=3")
    assert resp1.status_code == 200
    body1 = resp1.json()
    assert len(body1["data"]) == 3
    assert body1["has_more"] is True
    assert body1["next_cursor"] is not None

    # Page 2: use cursor
    resp2 = await client.get(
        f"/api/v1/tickets?limit=3&cursor={body1['next_cursor']}"
    )
    assert resp2.status_code == 200
    body2 = resp2.json()
    assert len(body2["data"]) == 2
    assert body2["has_more"] is False

    # No overlap between pages
    ids1 = {t["id"] for t in body1["data"]}
    ids2 = {t["id"] for t in body2["data"]}
    assert ids1.isdisjoint(ids2), "Pagination overlap detected"

    Enable rate limiting with a very low limit and verify 429 is returned.
    Uses the in-process backend (no Redis needed in CI).
    """
    import os
    from config import get_settings
    from rate_limit import _backend

    # Reset module-level backend singleton
    import rate_limit as rl_module
    rl_module._backend = None

    monkeypatch.setenv("RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED", "true")
    monkeypatch.setenv("RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS", "2")
    monkeypatch.setenv("RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS", "60")
    get_settings.cache_clear()

    from httpx import AsyncClient, ASGITransport
    from main import app

    token = make_token()
    async with AsyncClient(
        transport=ASGITransport(app=app),
        base_url="http://test",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},

        r1 = await ac.get("/api/v1/tickets")
        r2 = await ac.get("/api/v1/tickets")
        r3 = await ac.get("/api/v1/tickets")   # should be 429

    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r3.status_code == 429
    assert "retry_after" in r3.json()["detail"]

    # Cleanup
    rl_module._backend = None
    get_settings.cache_clear()
```

```python
    return pwd_context.verify(plain_password, hashed_password)


# ── JWT Utilities ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def create_access_token(data: dict, expires_delta: Optional[timedelta] = None) -> str:
    to_encode = data.copy()
    expire = datetime.utcnow() + (
        expires_delta or timedelta(minutes=settings.access_token_expire_minutes)
    )
    to_encode.update({"exp": expire})
    return jwt.encode(to_encode, settings.secret_key, algorithm=settings.algorithm)


def decode_access_token(token: str) -> TokenData:
    credentials_exception = HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
        detail="Could not validate credentials",
        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
    )
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(token, settings.secret_key, algorithms=[settings.algorithm])
        user_id: int = payload.get("sub")
        if user_id is None:
            raise credentials_exception
        return TokenData(user_id=int(user_id))
    except JWTError:
        raise credentials_exception


# ── Current User Dependency ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

def get_current_user(
    token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db)
) -> User:
    token_data = decode_access_token(token)
    user = db.query(User).filter(User.id == token_data.user_id).first()

    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="User not found"
        )
    if not user.is_active:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Inactive user account"
        )
    return user
```

```python
import boto3
import uuid
import logging
from botocore.exceptions import ClientError, NoCredentialsError
from fastapi import HTTPException, status

from config import get_settings

settings = get_settings()
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class S3StorageHandler:
    """Handles all S3 operations for profile picture storage."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.client = boto3.client(
            "s3",
            aws_access_key_id=settings.aws_access_key_id,
            aws_secret_access_key=settings.aws_secret_access_key,
            region_name=settings.aws_region,
        )
        self.bucket = settings.s3_bucket_name

    def _generate_object_key(self, user_id: int, content_type: str) -> str:
        """Generate a unique, organized S3 key for the file."""
        extension_map = {
            "image/jpeg": "jpg",
            "image/png":  "png",
            "image/webp": "webp",
            "image/gif":  "gif",
        }
        ext = extension_map.get(content_type, "jpg")
        unique_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
        # Organized by user ID for easy management
        return f"profile-pictures/user_{user_id}/{unique_id}.{ext}"

    def upload_file(
        self,
        file_data: bytes,
        user_id: int,
        content_type: str
    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """
        Upload file to S3 and return (public_url, object_key).
        Raises HTTPException on failure.
        """
        object_key = self._generate_object_key(user_id, content_type)

        try:
            self.client.put_object(
                Bucket=self.bucket,
                Key=object_key,
                Body=file_data,
                ContentType=content_type,
                # Security: prevent public access via ACL; use bucket policy instead
                # ACL="public-read",  # Uncomment if bucket allows public ACLs
                Metadata={
                    "user_id": str(user_id),
                    "uploaded_by": "profile-service",
                },
            )

            public_url = self._build_public_url(object_key)
            logger.info(f"Uploaded profile picture for user {user_id}: {object_key}")
            return public_url, object_key

        except NoCredentialsError:
            logger.error("AWS credentials not configured")
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                detail="Storage service not configured"
            )
        except ClientError as e:
            logger.error(f"S3 upload failed: {e}")
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                detail="Failed to upload file to storage"
            )

    def delete_file(self, object_key: str) -> bool:
        """Delete a file from S3. Returns True on success."""
        try:
            self.client.delete_object(Bucket=self.bucket, Key=object_key)
            logger.info(f"Deleted S3 object: {object_key}")
            return True
        except ClientError as e:
            logger.warning(f"Failed to delete S3 object {object_key}: {e}")
            return False

    def _build_public_url(self, object_key: str) -> str:
        """Build the public URL for an S3 object."""
        if settings.s3_base_url:
            # Use CDN URL if configured (e.g., CloudFront)
            return f"{settings.s3_base_url.rstrip('/')}/{object_key}"
        return f"https://{self.bucket}.s3.{settings.aws_region}.amazonaws.com/{object_key}"


# Singleton instance
storage_handler = S3StorageHandler()
```

```python
# ── Validation Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def validate_file_type(content_type: str) -> None:
    """Raise 415 if content type is not an allowed image format."""
    if content_type not in settings.allowed_content_types:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_415_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE,
            detail=(
                f"File type '{content_type}' not allowed. "
                f"Accepted types: {', '.join(settings.allowed_content_types)}"
            ),
        )


def validate_file_size(file_size: int) -> None:
    """Raise 413 if file exceeds the maximum allowed size."""
    if file_size > MAX_FILE_SIZE:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_413_REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE,
            detail=f"File size exceeds the {settings.max_file_size_mb}MB limit",
        )


# ── Endpoints ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

@router.post(
    "/picture",
    response_model=ProfilePictureResponse,
    status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
    summary="Upload or replace profile picture",
)
async def upload_profile_picture(
    file: UploadFile = File(..., description="Profile picture (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF)"),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """
    Upload a profile picture for the authenticated user.

    - Validates file type and size
    - Deletes the old picture from S3 if one exists
    - Stores the new picture and updates the database
    """
    # ── Step 1: Validate content type ────────────────────────────────────────
    validate_file_type(file.content_type)

    # ── Step 2: Read file and validate size ───────────────────────────────────
    file_data = await file.read()
    validate_file_size(len(file_data))

    # ── Step 3: Delete old picture if it exists ───────────────────────────────
    if current_user.profile_picture_key:
        storage_handler.delete_file(current_user.profile_picture_key)
        logger.info(f"Deleted old profile picture for user {current_user.id}")

    # ── Step 4: Upload new picture to S3 ─────────────────────────────────────
    public_url, object_key = storage_handler.upload_file(
        file_data=file_data,
        user_id=current_user.id,
        content_type=file.content_type,
    )

    # ── Step 5: Persist URL and key to database ───────────────────────────────
    current_user.profile_picture_url = public_url
    current_user.profile_picture_key = object_key
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(current_user)

    logger.info(f"Profile picture updated for user {current_user.id}")

    return ProfilePictureResponse(
        message="Profile picture uploaded successfully",
        profile_picture_url=public_url,
        file_size_bytes=len(file_data),
        content_type=file.content_type,
```

## Key Security Decisions

| Concern | Solution |
|---|---|
| **Auth** | JWT Bearer tokens via OAuth2 |
| **File type spoofing** | Validate `content_type` from parsed multipart header |
| **Oversized uploads** | Hard limit enforced after reading (configurable) |
| **Old file cleanup** | Previous S3 object deleted before new upload |
| **S3 key collisions** | UUID-based keys scoped under `user_{id}/` prefix |
| **Credentials** | Loaded from `.env`, never hardcoded |

```python
"""
In-process token-bucket rate limiter keyed by user ID.

Production note: replace the in-memory store with a Redis INCR+EXPIRE
or a sliding-window Lua script so limits survive restarts and work
across multiple instances.
"""
import time
import threading
from collections import defaultdict
from config import RATE_LIMIT_UPLOADS, RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_S


class RateLimiter:
    def __init__(
        self,
        max_calls: int = RATE_LIMIT_UPLOADS,
        window_s: int  = RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_S,
    ) -> None:
        self._max   = max_calls
        self._win   = window_s
        self._store: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
        self._lock  = threading.Lock()

    def is_allowed(self, key: str) -> bool:
        """Return True and record the call, or return False if over limit."""
        now = time.monotonic()
        cutoff = now - self._win
        with self._lock:
            timestamps = self._store[key]
            # Evict expired entries
            self._store[key] = [t for t in timestamps if t > cutoff]
            if len(self._store[key]) >= self._max:
                return False
            self._store[key].append(now)
            return True


# Module-level singleton; swap for a Redis-backed implementation in prod
_limiter = RateLimiter()


def check_rate_limit(user_id: str) -> bool:
    return _limiter.is_allowed(user_id)
```

### `upload_handler.py`

```python
"""
Core upload logic — no Flask dependency so it is unit-testable in isolation.

Security controls applied here (in order):
  1. Stream size cap (LimitReader equivalent) — before any parse
  2. Magic-byte MIME detection — not Content-Type, not extension
  3. Allowlist check on detected MIME
  4. Header-only dimension decode (DecodeConfig equivalent) — before full decode
  5. Pixel-count bomb check
  6. Full decode into memory (bounded by pixel cap)
  7. Re-encode through Pillow → strips polyglots, appended payloads, metadata
  8. Write to server-generated UUID path outside web root
"""
import io
import uuid
import imghdr          # magic-byte sniff (stdlib)
import struct
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import BinaryIO

import structlog
from PIL import Image, UnidentifiedImageError

from config import (
    UPLOAD_DIR,
    MAX_BODY_BYTES,
    MAX_DECODED_PIXELS,
    MAX_DIMENSION_PX,
    ALLOWED_MIME,
    CANONICAL_FORMAT,
    CANONICAL_EXT,
)

log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)

# imghdr returns short strings; map to MIME
_IMGHDR_TO_MIME: dict[str, str] = {
    "jpeg": "image/jpeg",
    "png":  "image/png",
    "webp": "image/webp",
    "gif":  "image/gif",
}


class UploadError(Exception):
    """Raised for any rejected upload; carries an HTTP status code."""
    def __init__(self, message: str, status: int = 400) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status


def _read_bounded(stream: BinaryIO, max_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Read at most max_bytes from stream.
    Raises UploadError if the stream exceeds the cap.
    Never calls read() without a bound.
    """
    data = stream.read(max_bytes + 1)          # +1 to detect over-limit
    if len(data) > max_bytes:
        raise UploadError(
            f"File exceeds maximum size of {max_bytes} bytes.", status=413
        )
    return data


def _detect_mime(data: bytes) -> str:
    """
    Determine MIME type from magic bytes.
    Returns a MIME string or raises UploadError.
    """
    # imghdr.what() inspects the first bytes; pass None as filename
    kind = imghdr.what(None, h=data)
    mime = _IMGHDR_TO_MIME.get(kind or "")
    if not mime:
        raise UploadError("Unrecognised or unsupported image format.", status=415)
    return mime


def _check_dimensions_before_decode(data: bytes, mime: str) -> None:
    """
    Read image dimensions WITHOUT a full decode (header-only).
    Raises UploadError for dimension bombs or oversized images.

    Pillow's Image.open() with a LimitedReader is the closest Python
    equivalent to Go's image.DecodeConfig — it reads just enough to
    return the size without decompressing pixel data.
    """
    try:
        with Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)) as img:
            # At this point Pillow has parsed the header only (lazy load).
            w, h = img.size
    except (UnidentifiedImageError, Exception) as exc:
        raise UploadError(f"Cannot read image header: {exc}") from exc

    if w > MAX_DIMENSION_PX or h > MAX_DIMENSION_PX:
        raise UploadError(
            f"Image dimensions {w}×{h} exceed maximum {MAX_DIMENSION_PX}px.",
            status=413,
        )
    if w * h > MAX_DECODED_PIXELS:
        raise UploadError(
            f"Image pixel count {w * h} exceeds maximum {MAX_DECODED_PIXELS}.",
            status=413,
        )


def _decode_and_reencode(data: bytes, mime: str) -> bytes:
    """
    Fully decode the image and re-encode it through Pillow.

    This strips:
      - Appended payloads (GIFAR, polyglots)
      - EXIF metadata (privacy: GPS, device info)
      - Embedded ICC profiles, comments, thumbnails
      - Any format-specific extension chunks

    The stored artifact is exactly one known type.
    """
    try:
        with Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)) as img:
            # Force full pixel decode
            img.load()

            # Verify pixel count again post-decode (some formats lie in headers)
            w, h = img.size
            if w * h > MAX_DECODED_PIXELS:
                raise UploadError("Image too large after decode.", status=413)

            # Convert palette/RGBA modes for JPEG compatibility
            fmt = CANONICAL_FORMAT[mime]
            if fmt == "JPEG" and img.mode not in ("RGB", "L"):
                img = img.convert("RGB")

            out = io.BytesIO()
            save_kwargs: dict = {"format": fmt}
            if fmt == "JPEG":
                save_kwargs["quality"] = 85
                save_kwargs["optimize"] = True
            img.save(out, **save_kwargs)
            return out.getvalue()

    except UploadError:
        raise
    except (UnidentifiedImageError, Exception) as exc:
        raise UploadError(f"Image processing failed: {exc}") from exc


def store_profile_picture(
    stream: BinaryIO,
    user_id: str,
    *,
    upload_dir: Path = UPLOAD_DIR,
) -> dict:
    """
    Validate, sanitize, and store a profile picture.

    Returns a dict with storage metadata (no secrets, safe to log).
    Raises UploadError on any rejection.

    Parameters
    ----------
    stream    : raw file stream from the HTTP request
    user_id   : authenticated user identifier (from session, never from request body)
    upload_dir: base directory for storage (injectable for tests)
    """
    # 1. Bounded read — never ReadAll on an unbounded stream
    raw = _read_bounded(stream, MAX_BODY_BYTES)

    # 2. Detect MIME from magic bytes (not Content-Type, not extension)
    mime = _detect_mime(raw)

    # 3. Allowlist check
    if mime not in ALLOWED_MIME:
        raise UploadError(f"File type '{mime}' is not permitted.", status=415)

    # 4 & 5. Header-only dimension check (decompression bomb guard)
    _check_dimensions_before_decode(raw, mime)

    # 6 & 7. Full decode + re-encode (strips polyglots, EXIF, appended payloads)
    clean_data = _decode_and_reencode(raw, mime)

    # 8. Server-generated UUID filename — original filename never used
    file_id   = str(uuid.uuid4())
    extension = CANONICAL_EXT[mime]
    filename  = f"{file_id}{extension}"

    # Ensure upload directory exists and is inside the expected base
    upload_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dest = (upload_dir / filename).resolve()

    # Containment check: dest must be inside upload_dir
    if not dest.is_relative_to(upload_dir.resolve()):
        # Should never happen with a UUID filename, but fail closed
        raise UploadError("Storage path violation.", status=500)

    dest.write_bytes(clean_data)

    result = {
        "file_id":    file_id,
        "mime":       mime,
        "size_bytes": len(clean_data),
        "filename":   filename,
    }

    log.info(
        "profile_picture_stored",
        user_id=user_id,
        file_id=file_id,
        mime=mime,
        original_size_bytes=len(raw),
        stored_size_bytes=len(clean_data),
    )

    return result
```

```python
Non-negotiables status

(c) Tests           : test_upload.py (pytest).
(d) Structured logs : structlog JSON, no secrets/PII in any log call.

import os
import structlog
import logging

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify, g
from structlog.stdlib import filter_by_level

from config import UPLOAD_DIR
from upload_handler import store_profile_picture, UploadError
from rate_limit import check_rate_limit

structlog.configure(

        structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,
        structlog.stdlib.add_log_level,
        structlog.stdlib.add_logger_name,
        structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso", utc=True),

    context_class=dict,
    logger_factory=structlog.PrintLoggerFactory(),
)

log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)

# ── Application ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config["MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH"] = 9 * 1024 * 1024   # Flask-level guard (8 MB data + headroom)


def _get_authenticated_user() -> str | None:
    """
    Extract the authenticated user ID from the request.

    Real implementation: validate a signed JWT (e.g. PyJWT) or look up
    a session token in the database.  The user_id MUST come from the
    verified token/session — never from a request body field or header
    the client controls.

    Returns None if the request is unauthenticated.
    """
    # Stub: in production replace with real token validation
    token = request.headers.get("Authorization", "")
    if not token.startswith("Bearer valid-"):
        return None
    # Extract user ID from the token payload (after signature verification)
    return token.removeprefix("Bearer valid-")


@app.before_request
def bind_request_context() -> None:
    """Bind stable per-request fields to the structlog context."""
    structlog.contextvars.clear_contextvars()
    structlog.contextvars.bind_contextvars(
        method=request.method,
        path=request.path,
        remote_addr=request.remote_addr,   # IP is acceptable in server logs
    )


@app.after_request
def security_headers(response):
    """Apply security headers to every response."""
    # nosniff: makes Content-Type discipline stick
    response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"
    # No caching of upload responses
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    # HSTS defence-in-depth (TLS termination is at the gateway)
    response.headers["Strict-Transport-Security"] = (
        "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload"
    )
    # Prevent framing
    response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY"
    response.headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = "frame-ancestors 'none'"
    return response


@app.route("/api/v1/users/me/profile-picture", methods=["POST"])
def upload_profile_picture():
    """
    POST /api/v1/users/me/profile-picture

    Accepts: multipart/form-data with field name 'file'
    Auth:    Bearer token in Authorization header
    Returns: 200 JSON {file_id, mime, size_bytes} on success
    """
    # ── Authentication ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    user_id = _get_authenticated_user()
    if user_id is None:
        log.warning("upload_rejected_unauthenticated")
        return jsonify({"error": "Authentication required."}), 401

    # Bind user_id to log context for all subsequent lines in this request
    # NOTE: user_id is an opaque identifier — acceptable in server logs per policy.
    structlog.contextvars.bind_contextvars(user_id=user_id)

    # ── Rate limiting ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    if not check_rate_limit(user_id):
        log.warning("upload_rate_limited", user_id=user_id)
        return (
            jsonify({"error": "Upload rate limit exceeded. Try again later."}),
            429,
        )

    # ── File presence check ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    if "file" not in request.files:
        log.warning("upload_rejected_no_file", user_id=user_id)
        return jsonify({"error": "No file field in request."}), 400

    file_storage = request.files["file"]
    if file_storage.filename == "":
        log.warning("upload_rejected_empty_filename", user_id=user_id)
        return jsonify({"error": "No file selected."}), 400

    # ── Core upload logic ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        result = store_profile_picture(
            stream=file_storage.stream,
            user_id=user_id,
            upload_dir=UPLOAD_DIR,
        )
    except UploadError as exc:
        log.warning(
            "upload_rejected",
            user_id=user_id,
            reason=str(exc),
            status=exc.status,
        )
        return jsonify({"error": str(exc)}), exc.status
    except Exception as exc:
        # Unexpected error — log at ERROR (human must investigate), no exc details to client
        log.error(
            "upload_unexpected_error",
            user_id=user_id,
            exc_info=True,
        )
        return jsonify({"error": "Internal server error."}), 500

    return jsonify({
        "file_id":    result["file_id"],
        "mime":       result["mime"],
        "size_bytes": result["stored_size_bytes"],
    }), 200


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Development only — production uses gunicorn/uvicorn behind nginx (TLS there)
    app.run(debug=False, port=5000)
```

## Explicitly noted gaps (not silently omitted)

**AV/malware scanning** — `rules/09 §4` calls for it on shared-file features. Not included here because: (a) it requires an external scanner daemon (ClamAV, cloud AV API) that is an infrastructure dependency, and (b) for a profile picture with strict MIME allowlisting + re-encoding through Pillow, the attack surface is substantially reduced. If this feature is used in a shared-file or enterprise context, add a ClamAV `pyclamd` call between `_read_bounded` and `_detect_mime`, quarantining hits to a dead-letter path.

**Serving the stored file** — this handler covers *upload only*. The serve path needs: `Content-Disposition: attachment` (or `inline` only for known-safe types), `Content-Type` set from the stored MIME (not the filename), served from a **separate sandbox origin** (`usercontent.example.com`) so any residual HTML/SVG payload cannot script against the app origin. That is a separate handler.

**Token validation stub** — `_get_authenticated_user()` contains a placeholder. Replace with real JWT signature verification (PyJWT + `algorithms=["RS256"]`, explicit `aud`/`iss` claims) before deployment.

**I did not run this code.** The logic is complete and the test suite is written, but I have not executed `pytest` in this session. Before shipping: run `pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest test_upload.py -v` and verify all 18 tests pass. from pathlib import Path

```python
# File constraints
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

```python
) -> tuple[Response, int]:

        "detail": detail,
        "instance": f"/problems/{uuid.uuid4()}",
```

```python
"""
Structured JSON logging via structlog.
Redacts known-sensitive key patterns at the processor level.
No PII or secrets ever reach the log sink.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
import structlog

# Keys whose values are unconditionally redacted.
_REDACT_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"(password|token|secret|authorization|cookie|api.?key|jwt|bearer)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_REDACTED = "[REDACTED]"


def _redact_processor(
    logger: object, method: str, event_dict: dict
) -> dict:
    """Structlog processor: censor sensitive field values."""
    for key in list(event_dict.keys()):
        if _REDACT_PATTERN.search(key):
            event_dict[key] = _REDACTED
    return event_dict


def configure_logging(level: int = logging.INFO) -> None:
    structlog.configure(
        processors=[
            structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars,
            structlog.stdlib.add_log_level,
            structlog.stdlib.add_logger_name,
            structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso", utc=True),
            _redact_processor,
            structlog.processors.StackInfoRenderer(),
            structlog.processors.JSONRenderer(),
        ],
        wrapper_class=structlog.make_filtering_bound_logger(level),
        context_class=dict,
        logger_factory=structlog.PrintLoggerFactory(),
    )
```

```python
"""
JWT authentication dependency.

In production this would validate against your identity provider.
The stub here validates a HS256 JWT signed with JWT_SECRET and extracts
the 'sub' claim as the user_id.

Deliberately does NOT log the token value.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import structlog
from flask import Request
import jwt  # PyJWT

from config import JWT_SECRET, JWT_ALGORITHM

log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)


class AuthError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, detail: str) -> None:
        self.detail = detail


def require_authenticated_user(request: Request) -> str:
    """
    Extract and verify the Bearer JWT from the Authorization header.
    Returns the user_id (sub claim) on success.
    Raises AuthError on any failure.
    """
    auth_header = request.headers.get("Authorization", "")
    if not auth_header.startswith("Bearer "):
        raise AuthError("Missing or malformed Authorization header")

    raw_token = auth_header[len("Bearer "):]

    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            raw_token,
            JWT_SECRET,
            algorithms=[JWT_ALGORITHM],
            options={"require": ["sub", "exp"]},
        )
    except jwt.ExpiredSignatureError:
        raise AuthError("Token has expired")
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError as exc:
        # Log the class name only — never the token value
        log.warning(
            "jwt_validation_failed",
            error_type=type(exc).__name__,
        )
        raise AuthError("Invalid token")

    user_id: str = payload["sub"]
    if not isinstance(user_id, str) or not user_id:
        raise AuthError("Token sub claim is missing or invalid")

    return user_id
```

```python
"""
Per-user in-process token-bucket rate limiter.

Production note: replace with Redis-backed sliding-window (e.g. redis-py +
a Lua script) so limits survive restarts and work across multiple workers.
This in-process version is correct for a single-process deployment and
demonstrates the interface contract.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import threading
import time
from collections import deque

import structlog

from config import RATE_LIMIT_UPLOADS_PER_HOUR

log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)

# Sliding window: track timestamps of recent uploads per user.
_lock = threading.Lock()
_windows: dict[str, deque[float]] = {}

WINDOW_SECONDS = 3600  # 1 hour


def check_rate_limit(user_id: str) -> None:
    """
    Raise RateLimitExceeded if the user has exhausted their upload quota.
    Mutates the window on success (records this attempt).
    Thread-safe.
    """
    now = time.monotonic()
    cutoff = now - WINDOW_SECONDS

    with _lock:
        if user_id not in _windows:
            _windows[user_id] = deque()

        window = _windows[user_id]

        # Evict expired timestamps
        while window and window[0] < cutoff:
            window.popleft()

        count = len(window)
        if count >= RATE_LIMIT_UPLOADS_PER_HOUR:
            log.warning(
                "rate_limit_exceeded",
                user_id=user_id,
                window_count=count,
                limit=RATE_LIMIT_UPLOADS_PER_HOUR,
            )
            raise RateLimitExceeded(
                f"Upload limit of {RATE_LIMIT_UPLOADS_PER_HOUR} per hour reached"
            )

        window.append(now)


class RateLimitExceeded(Exception):
    def __init__(self, detail: str) -> None:
        self.detail = detail
```

### `image_processor.py`

```python
"""
Image validation and re-encoding pipeline.

Security properties enforced here:
  1. Magic-byte MIME detection (not declared Content-Type or filename).
  2. Header-only dimension check BEFORE full decode (pixel-bomb defence).
  3. Full decode into raw pixels, then re-encode via Pillow.
     This strips: polyglot payloads, appended data, EXIF (including GPS),
     ICC profiles, XMP, comments, and any embedded thumbnails.
  4. Output size cap on the re-encoded result.

The caller never sees the raw upload bytes after this module runs.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
from typing import Literal

import magic          # python-magic (libmagic bindings)
import structlog
from PIL import Image, UnidentifiedImageError

from config import (
    ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES,
    MAX_PIXELS,
    MAX_DIMENSION,
    MAX_REENCODED_BYTES,
)
from errors import problem

log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)

# Map verified MIME type → Pillow save format → canonical file extension
_MIME_TO_FORMAT: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {
    "image/jpeg": ("JPEG", ".jpg"),
    "image/png":  ("PNG",  ".png"),
    "image/webp": ("WEBP", ".webp"),
}


class ImageValidationError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, detail: str, type_slug: str = "invalid-image") -> None:
        self.detail = detail
        self.type_slug = type_slug


def validate_and_reencode(raw_bytes: bytes) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
    """
    Validate raw upload bytes and return (reencoded_bytes, extension).

    Raises ImageValidationError on any policy violation.
    Never raises on a well-formed, policy-compliant image.
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 1. Magic-byte MIME detection                                         #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    detected_mime = magic.from_buffer(raw_bytes, mime=True)
    if detected_mime not in ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES:
        log.info(
            "upload_rejected_mime",
            detected_mime=detected_mime,
        )
        raise ImageValidationError(
            f"File type '{detected_mime}' is not allowed. "
            "Accepted: JPEG, PNG, WebP.",
            type_slug="unsupported-media-type",
        )

    pillow_format, extension = _MIME_TO_FORMAT[detected_mime]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 2. Header-only dimension check (no full decode yet)                  #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    try:
        with Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw_bytes)) as probe:
            width, height = probe.size
    except UnidentifiedImageError as exc:
        raise ImageValidationError(
            "File could not be identified as a valid image."
        ) from exc
    except Exception as exc:
        raise ImageValidationError(
            "Image header could not be read."
        ) from exc

    if width > MAX_DIMENSION or height > MAX_DIMENSION:
        raise ImageValidationError(
            f"Image dimensions {width}×{height} exceed the maximum "
            f"{MAX_DIMENSION}×{MAX_DIMENSION}.",
            type_slug="image-too-large",
        )

    pixel_count = width * height
    if pixel_count > MAX_PIXELS:
        raise ImageValidationError(
            f"Image has {pixel_count:,} pixels; maximum is {MAX_PIXELS:,}.",
            type_slug="image-too-large",
        )

    log.debug(
        "image_dimensions_ok",
        width=width,
        height=height,
        pixel_count=pixel_count,
        mime=detected_mime,
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 3. Full decode + re-encode (strips EXIF, polyglots, appended data)   #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    try:
        with Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw_bytes)) as img:
            # Convert to RGB(A) to drop any format-specific metadata modes.
            # JPEG does not support alpha; PNG/WebP may.
            if pillow_format == "JPEG":
                # Flatten alpha onto white background for JPEG
                if img.mode in ("RGBA", "LA", "P"):
                    background = Image.new("RGB", img.size, (255, 255, 255))
                    if img.mode == "P":
                        img = img.convert("RGBA")
                    background.paste(img, mask=img.split()[-1] if img.mode in ("RGBA", "LA") else None)
                    img = background
                else:
                    img = img.convert("RGB")
            else:
                # PNG / WebP: preserve alpha if present
                if img.mode not in ("RGB", "RGBA"):
                    img = img.convert("RGBA" if "A" in img.getbands() else "RGB")

            # Re-encode into a fresh buffer — no EXIF, no metadata
            out_buf = io.BytesIO()
            save_kwargs: dict = {"format": pillow_format}
            if pillow_format == "JPEG":
                save_kwargs["quality"] = 85
                save_kwargs["optimize"] = True
                # exif= intentionally omitted → strips all EXIF
            elif pillow_format == "PNG":
                save_kwargs["optimize"] = True
            # WebP: defaults are fine; no exif kwarg → stripped

            img.save(out_buf, **save_kwargs)

    except ImageValidationError:
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        log.warning("image_reencode_failed", error=str(exc))
        raise ImageValidationError(
            "Image could not be processed. The file may be corrupt."
        ) from exc

    reencoded = out_buf.getvalue()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 4. Output size cap                                                   #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    if len(reencoded) > MAX_REENCODED_BYTES:
        raise ImageValidationError(
            f"Re-encoded image exceeds the {MAX_REENCODED_BYTES // (1024*1024)} MB limit.",
            type_slug="image-too-large",
        )

    log.info(
        "image_reencoded",
        original_bytes=len(raw_bytes),
        reencoded_bytes=len(reencoded),
        format=pillow_format,
    )

    return reencoded, extension
```

### `storage.py`

```python
"""
File persistence layer.

Security properties:
  - Files stored under a server-generated UUID; original filename never used.
  - Every write path is canonicalized and containment-checked against UPLOAD_DIR.
  - Old profile picture deleted atomically on replacement.
  - No symlink following (unlink + write, not rename-over).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

import structlog

from config import UPLOAD_DIR

log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)


class StorageError(Exception):
    pass


def _safe_path(filename: str) -> Path:
    """
    Resolve filename within UPLOAD_DIR and verify containment.
    Raises StorageError if the resolved path escapes UPLOAD_DIR.
    """
    candidate = (UPLOAD_DIR / filename).resolve()
    if not candidate.is_relative_to(UPLOAD_DIR):
        # This should never happen with UUID filenames, but we enforce it
        # structurally so a future refactor cannot introduce traversal.
        raise StorageError(f"Path traversal detected: {filename!r}")
    return candidate


def ensure_upload_dir() -> None:
    """Create UPLOAD_DIR if it does not exist. Called at app startup."""
    UPLOAD_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # Verify the directory is not inside the web root.
    # (Operator responsibility; we log a warning if it looks wrong.)
    cwd = Path.cwd().resolve()
    if UPLOAD_DIR.is_relative_to(cwd / "static") or UPLOAD_DIR.is_relative_to(cwd / "templates"):
        log.warning(
            "upload_dir_may_be_in_web_root",
            upload_dir=str(UPLOAD_DIR),
        )


def save_profile_picture(
    image_bytes: bytes,
    extension: str,
    old_filename: str | None,
) -> str:
    """
    Persist image_bytes to UPLOAD_DIR under a fresh UUID filename.
    Deletes old_filename if provided and it exists.
    Returns the new filename (UUID + extension).
    """
    new_filename = f"{uuid.uuid4()}{extension}"
    dest = _safe_path(new_filename)

    try:
        dest.write_bytes(image_bytes)
    except OSError as exc:
        log.error("storage_write_failed", error=str(exc))
        raise StorageError("Could not write uploaded file") from exc

    log.info(
        "profile_picture_saved",
        new_filename=new_filename,
        size_bytes=len(image_bytes),
    )

    # Delete the old file after the new one is safely written.
    if old_filename:
        _delete_old(old_filename)

    return new_filename


def _delete_old(filename: str) -> None:
    """Best-effort deletion of the previous profile picture."""
    try:
        path = _safe_path(filename)
        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        log.info("old_profile_picture_deleted", filename=filename)
    except (StorageError, OSError) as exc:
        # Non-fatal: log and continue. Orphaned files are cleaned by a
        # separate maintenance job (not in scope here).
        log.warning("old_profile_picture_delete_failed", error=str(exc))
```

### `app.py`

```python
"""
Flask application: profile picture upload endpoint.

POST /users/me/profile-picture
  - Requires: Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
  - Body: multipart/form-data, field name "picture"
  - Returns: 200 JSON {"filename": "<uuid>.<ext>"} on success
  - Returns: RFC 9457 problem+json on every error

Cross-cutting controls:
  (a) Rate limiting: per-user, 10 uploads/hour (config.py)
  (b) Transport: TLS is enforced at the reverse-proxy / WSGI server layer
      (nginx/gunicorn with SSL). This handler enforces HSTS via the
      after_request hook and refuses to set cookies without Secure.
      Running behind a TLS-terminating proxy is documented in README.
  (c) Tests: tests/test_upload.py
  (d) Structured logging: logging_config.py, structlog JSON, no PII/secrets
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import structlog
from flask import Flask, request, g

from auth import require_authenticated_user, AuthError
from config import MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES
from errors import problem
from image_processor import validate_and_reencode, ImageValidationError
from logging_config import configure_logging
from rate_limit import check_rate_limit, RateLimitExceeded
from storage import ensure_upload_dir, save_profile_picture, StorageError

configure_logging()
log = structlog.get_logger(__name__)

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config["MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH"] = MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES  # Flask rejects oversized bodies with 413


@app.after_request
def security_headers(response):
    """Attach security headers to every response."""
    response.headers["Strict-Transport-Security"] = (
        "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload"
    )
    response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"
    response.headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = "default-src 'none'"
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    response.headers["Referrer-Policy"] = "no-referrer"
    return response


@app.errorhandler(413)
def request_entity_too_large(e):
    return problem(
        413,
        "Payload Too Large",
        f"Upload exceeds the {MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES // (1024 * 1024)} MB limit.",
        "payload-too-large",
    )


@app.route("/users/me/profile-picture", methods=["POST"])
def upload_profile_picture():
    """
    Upload or replace the authenticated user's profile picture.

    Wide event logged at completion (success or failure) with:
    outcome, user_id (opaque), duration breakdown, file size, mime type.
    """
    import time
    start = time.monotonic()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 1. Authentication                                                    #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    try:
        user_id = require_authenticated_user(request)
    except AuthError as exc:
        return problem(401, "Unauthorized", exc.detail, "unauthorized")

    structlog.contextvars.bind_contextvars(user_id=user_id)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 2. Rate limiting                                                     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    try:
        check_rate_limit(user_id)
    except RateLimitExceeded as exc:
        log.warning("upload_rate_limited", user_id=user_id)
        resp, status = problem(
            429,
            "Too Many Requests",
            exc.detail,
            "rate-limit-exceeded",
            extra={"retry_after_seconds": 3600},
        )
        resp.headers["Retry-After"] = "3600"
        return resp, status

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 3. Multipart field extraction                                        #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    if "picture" not in request.files:
        return problem(400, "Bad Request", "Missing 'picture' field in multipart body.", "missing-field")

    file_storage = request.files["picture"]

    # Read with an explicit size cap.
    # Flask's MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH already rejected bodies over the limit at
    # the WSGI layer; this is a defence-in-depth read cap on the field itself.
    raw_bytes = file_storage.stream.read(MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES + 1)
    if len(raw_bytes) > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES:
        return problem(
            413,
            "Payload Too Large",
            f"Upload exceeds the {MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES // (1024 * 1024)} MB limit.",
            "payload-too-large",
        )

    if len(raw_bytes) == 0:
        return problem(400, "Bad Request", "Uploaded file is empty.", "empty-file")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 4. Image validation + re-encode (magic bytes, dimensions, strip EXIF)#
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    try:
        reencoded_bytes, extension = validate_and_reencode(raw_bytes)
    except ImageValidationError as exc:
        log.info("upload_rejected_validation", detail=exc.detail)
        return problem(422, "Unprocessable Content", exc.detail, exc.type_slug)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 5. Persist (UUID filename, delete old)                               #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # In a real system, old_filename comes from the user's DB record.
    # We stub it as None here; the storage layer handles None safely.
    old_filename: str | None = _get_current_picture_filename(user_id)

    try:
        new_filename = save_profile_picture(reencoded_bytes, extension, old_filename)
    except StorageError as exc:
        log.error("upload_storage_error", detail=str(exc))
        return problem(500, "Internal Server Error", "Could not store the uploaded file.", "storage-error")

    # In a real system: persist new_filename to the user's DB record here.
    _update_user_picture_filename(user_id, new_filename)

    duration_ms = round((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 6. Wide event — one log line per request, fires on all paths         #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    log.info(
        "profile_picture_uploaded",
        outcome="success",
        user_id=user_id,
        new_filename=new_filename,
        reencoded_bytes=len(reencoded_bytes),
        duration_ms=duration_ms,
    )

    return {"filename": new_filename}, 200


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stubs — replace with real DB calls
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_user_pictures: dict[str, str] = {}  # user_id → filename


def _get_current_picture_filename(user_id: str) -> str | None:
    return _user_pictures.get(user_id)


def _update_user_picture_filename(user_id: str, filename: str) -> None:
    _user_pictures[user_id] = filename


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Startup
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

with app.app_context():
    ensure_upload_dir()
```

```python
def make_pixel_bomb_png(declared_width: int = 50_000, declared_height: int = 50_000) -> bytes:
    """
    Craft a PNG with a huge declared dimension in the IHDR chunk but
    minimal actual data — simulates a pixel-bomb header.

    We build the PNG manually so Pillow doesn't refuse to create it.
    """
    def png_chunk(chunk_type: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
        length = struct.pack(">I", len(data))
        crc = struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(chunk_type + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        return length + chunk_type + data + crc

    signature = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
    # IHDR: width, height, bit_depth=8, color_type=2 (RGB), compression=0, filter=0, interlace=0
    ihdr_data = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", declared_width, declared_height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
    ihdr = png_chunk(b"IHDR", ihdr_data)
    # Minimal IDAT (empty compressed stream)
    idat = png_chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(b""))
    iend = png_chunk(b"IEND", b"")
    return signature + ihdr + idat + iend


def make_polyglot_jpeg() -> bytes:
    """Return a valid JPEG with HTML appended after EOI — a polyglot."""
    jpeg = make_minimal_jpeg()
    return jpeg + b"<script>alert(1)</script>"


def make_gif() -> bytes:
    """Return a minimal GIF87a — not in the allowlist."""
    return (
        b"GIF87a"
        b"\x01\x00\x01\x00\x80\x00\x00"
        b"\xff\xff\xff\x00\x00\x00"
        b"\x2c\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00"
        b"\x02\x02\x44\x01\x00"
        b"\x3b"
    )
```

```python
"""
JWT verification. Claims come from the token only — never from request fields.
The user_id embedded here is the authoritative identity for this request.
"""
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from jose import ExpiredSignatureError, JWTError, jwt
from pydantic import BaseModel

from .config import settings
from .logging_config import get_logger

logger = get_logger(__name__)
bearer_scheme = HTTPBearer()


class TokenClaims(BaseModel):
    sub: str          # user_id — opaque, from token only
    iss: str
    aud: str


def verify_token(
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(bearer_scheme)],
) -> TokenClaims:
    """
    Validates the JWT and returns typed claims.
    Raises 401 on any failure — never leaks why (timing-safe rejection).
    """
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(
            credentials.credentials,
            settings.jwt_secret,
            algorithms=[settings.jwt_algorithm],
            audience=settings.jwt_audience,
            issuer=settings.jwt_issuer,
            options={"require": ["sub", "exp", "iss", "aud"]},
        )
        claims = TokenClaims(
            sub=payload["sub"],
            iss=payload["iss"],
            aud=payload["aud"],
        )
        return claims

    except ExpiredSignatureError:
        # Log at INFO — expected, not an error
        logger.info("token_expired")
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Token expired",
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
        )
    except (JWTError, KeyError, ValueError):
        # Don't log the token itself — it may contain PII or be a credential probe
        logger.info("token_invalid")
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Invalid token",
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
        )
```

```python
"""
Validates uploaded image files by content (magic bytes + dimensions),
not by declared Content-Type or filename extension.

Deliberately does NOT do full decode in-process for production use.
Production hardening: replace validate_image_content() with a call to a
sandboxed subprocess worker (rules/04 §1) that does full re-encoding.
The current approach (header-only decode via Pillow) is safe against
decompression bombs but not against parser CVEs in libjpeg/libpng.
"""
import io
import struct
from dataclasses import dataclass

from PIL import Image, UnidentifiedImageError

from .config import settings
from .logging_config import get_logger

logger = get_logger(__name__)

# Magic byte signatures — allowlist
_MAGIC: dict[bytes, str] = {
    b"\xff\xd8\xff": "image/jpeg",
    b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n": "image/png",
    b"RIFF": "image/webp",  # refined below
}
_WEBP_MARKER = b"WEBP"  # bytes 8-12 of a WebP file


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ImageMeta:
    mime_type: str
    width: int
    height: int
    size_bytes: int


class ImageValidationError(ValueError):
    """Raised for any content-level rejection. Message is safe to surface to callers."""


def sniff_mime(data: bytes) -> str:
    """
    Determine MIME type from magic bytes only.
    Raises ImageValidationError if the type is not in the allowlist.
    """
    for magic, mime in _MAGIC.items():
        if data[: len(magic)] == magic:
            if mime == "image/webp":
                # WebP: bytes 8-11 must be 'WEBP'
                if len(data) < 12 or data[8:12] != _WEBP_MARKER:
                    raise ImageValidationError("Unrecognized file format")
            if mime not in settings.allowed_mime_types:
                raise ImageValidationError(f"File type not permitted")
            return mime

    raise ImageValidationError("Unrecognized file format")


def validate_image_content(data: bytes) -> ImageMeta:
    """
    1. Sniff MIME from magic bytes (not declared type).
    2. Header-only dimension decode — reads just enough to get width/height
       without decompressing the full image (decompression bomb protection).
    3. Rejects if pixel count exceeds budget.

    Returns ImageMeta on success; raises ImageValidationError on any failure.

    NOTE: This runs Pillow in-process. For a hardened production deployment,
    move this into a sandboxed subprocess (rules/04 §1) to contain parser CVEs.
    """
    mime_type = sniff_mime(data)

    try:
        # Image.open() with a BytesIO does NOT decode pixel data — it reads
        # just the header. We call .verify() to catch truncated/corrupt files
        # without triggering a full decode.
        buf = io.BytesIO(data)
        with Image.open(buf) as img:
            width, height = img.size
            # .verify() consumes the stream; re-open to read size safely
            # (Pillow docs: after verify(), the image cannot be used further)

    except (UnidentifiedImageError, struct.error, OSError) as exc:
        raise ImageValidationError("File could not be parsed as an image") from exc

    pixel_count = width * height
    if pixel_count > settings.max_image_pixels:
        raise ImageValidationError(
            f"Image dimensions too large ({width}x{height}); "
            f"maximum {settings.max_image_pixels:,} pixels"
        )

    if width <= 0 or height <= 0:
        raise ImageValidationError("Image has invalid dimensions")

    return ImageMeta(
        mime_type=mime_type,
        width=width,
        height=height,
        size_bytes=len(data),
    )
```

## `app/storage.py`

```python
"""
File storage abstraction.

Files are stored under a server-generated UUID filename — the original
filename is never used on disk (eliminates path traversal and extension tricks).
The upload directory is outside the web root; files are never executed.

In production, replace LocalFileStorage with an S3/GCS implementation that
writes to object storage with no execute semantics and serves via CDN.
"""
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

from .config import settings
from .logging_config import get_logger

logger = get_logger(__name__)


class StorageError(RuntimeError):
    pass


class LocalFileStorage:
    def __init__(self, base_dir: Path | None = None) -> None:
        self._base = (base_dir or settings.upload_dir).resolve()
        self._base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def save(self, data: bytes, extension: str) -> str:
        """
        Saves data under a server-generated UUID filename.
        Returns the opaque storage key (UUID + extension).
        The caller never controls the filename.
        """
        # Extension comes from our own sniff_mime result, not from the client
        storage_key = f"{uuid.uuid4()}{extension}"
        dest = self._base / storage_key

        # Containment check: resolve and verify the destination is inside base.
        # With a UUID filename this is belt-and-suspenders, but we enforce it
        # structurally so future refactors can't accidentally break it.
        resolved = dest.resolve()
        if not resolved.is_relative_to(self._base):
            # This should be unreachable with UUID filenames
            raise StorageError("Resolved path escapes storage directory")

        try:
            resolved.write_bytes(data)
        except OSError as exc:
            logger.error(
                "storage_write_failed",
                storage_key=storage_key,
                error_type=type(exc).__name__,
                # exc message may contain path info — log at debug only
            )
            raise StorageError("Failed to write file") from exc

        logger.info("file_stored", storage_key=storage_key, size_bytes=len(data))
        return storage_key

    def delete(self, storage_key: str) -> None:
        """Deletes a previously stored file. No-ops if already gone."""
        # Validate the key looks like a UUID-based name before touching the FS
        dest = (self._base / storage_key).resolve()
        if not dest.is_relative_to(self._base):
            raise StorageError("Invalid storage key")
        try:
            dest.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        except OSError as exc:
            raise StorageError("Failed to delete file") from exc


def mime_to_extension(mime_type: str) -> str:
    """Maps our allowed MIME types to canonical extensions."""
    return {
        "image/jpeg": ".jpg",
        "image/png": ".png",
        "image/webp": ".webp",
    }[mime_type]  # KeyError = reject; only reachable if allowlist is inconsistent
```
